Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets (recap and next steps)

Hi Claire — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have aligned acceptance gates for a Dedicated pilot:

Summary of what we heard (please correct if any of this is off):
- Workload: multi-turn customer support assistant with streaming token-level responses and tool calls to your internal search.
- Latency targets: p50 streaming partials < 60ms, p95 end-to-end response <= 250ms for non-long requests (<= 512 tokens).
- Throughput requirement: sustained 350 reqs/sec across peak window (US East), concurrency up to ~48 live sessions.
- Stability: failover to smaller model variant if GPU pool saturation occurs; expect 99.9% availability SLA during pilot window.

Our recommended pilot scope: 1) run a 72-hour smoke pilot using a 4-node reserved slab (H100 or A100 options) with continuous batching + KV caching enabled; 2) benchmark streaming tail latencies and p95 under your traffic shape; 3) validate rollout/fallback behavior and cost telemetry.

Attachments: I attached a short requirements summary and our GPU matrix (first pass) — Karthik and Priyom will follow up with concrete perf expectations by GPU type and a suggested pilot configuration.

Asks / next steps:
- Claire: confirm the representative traffic window (UTC times + sample volume) and a contact for procurement to provision a short-term PO for Dedicated pilot.
- Megan: if you can share procurement cadence and PO template, we can draft a one-month reserved pilot commitment and a statement of work.
- Karthik & Priyom: please add GPU tradeoffs + test plan.

I'll hold a 30-minute technical kickoff on Monday if that works (proposed: 2026-10-05 10:00 AM ET).

Thanks,

Subject: GPU comparison and expected perf envelope (first pass)

Hi all — following up with an engineer-oriented snapshot of tradeoffs between candidate GPU families for the pilot. This is intentionally frank — final numbers will change after we run your workload, but it helps set expectations.

Key assumptions: 3-token generation per step average for short flows, batch sizes tuned by the runtime, KV cache hit expected 60% on repeated conversational contexts. Payloads are mixed: 90% <=256 tokens, 10% long sessions.

High-level comparison (expected relative performance for your workload):
- H100 (80GB): best streaming tail behavior at lower batch sizes due to larger L2 and improved attention kernels; expect p95 streaming partials ~40–80ms with continuous batching tuned, and sustained throughput per GPU ~90–110 short reqs/sec (with batching).
- A100 (80GB): solid throughput for batched workloads; p95 streaming partials ~70–140ms depending on KV cache effectiveness; throughput per GPU ~70–95 short reqs/sec.
- L40S / L4-class (lower cost): good cost/throughput for non-tail-critical workloads — p95 might be 200–400ms under burst, throughput higher with larger batching but worse tail.

Prelim pilot config suggestions:
- Conservative (latency-first): 4x H100s reserved, continuous batching enabled, 3x autoscaling headroom for brief bursts.
- Balanced (cost/throughput): 6x A100s reserved with tighter batching and aggressive KV cache TTL.

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- Tail: p95 streaming partials for short flows <= 200ms and p50 <= 80ms.
- End-to-end: p95 non-long-responses <= 250ms.
- Throughput: sustained 350 reqs/sec in peak window for 1 hour at steady state with <=2% error rate and no more than 5% request queuing.
- Stability: can failover to smaller model variant without >2x increase in p95.

I'll attach a detailed bench matrix; Priyom will outline exact steps for the 72-hour smoke run and the metrics we'll consume (per-token latency, per-request wall clock, batching efficiency, KV hit ratio).

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-04T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot plan (MOP) + test harness and runbook

Claire / Megan — attaching the proposed method-of-procedure (pilot-mop.md) for the 72-hour Dedicated pilot. Highlights below and explicit asks so procurement can see scope.

Run steps (high level):
1) Provision reserved slab (option A: 4x H100; option B: 6x A100) in us-east-1 with private VPC peering to DeepDive.
2) Deploy chosen model variant pinned to a model version with streaming enabled; enable KV cache and prefix caching for hot sessions.
3) Warm-up: synthetic ramp to replicate your peak shape for 30 minutes, then run a 72-hour window capturing detailed telemetry.
4) Failure scenarios: simulate single node failure and model fallback to ensure graceful degradation.
5) Deliverables: perf report (p50/p95/p99 latency, batching efficiency, reserved throughput utilization), cost estimate, recommended production slab sizing.

Procurement asks for PO: pilot duration: 1 month reserved (we typically provide prorated credits if pilot shorter), estimated cost range: $XXk–$YYk depending on GPU choice and region (we'll provide a concrete number after you pick option A/B).

Data security: logs will be sent to your VPC S3 with customer-managed KMS keys. No user text stored outside your VPC.

Please confirm which GPU option you prefer for the smoke pilot and I'll loop in our CloudOps to start provisioning immediately once we have the PO.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-mop.md (runbook, 4 pages)
